title: Samson Carried a City Gate 60 km?
notes: Gaza-Hebron straight-line ~60 km. The 'facing Hebron' nuance (beat 6) is the single not-proven line.

beats.text: Samson carried a city gate how far?
Judges sixteen: at midnight, Samson lifts the doors of Gaza's gate.
He takes doors, posts and bar, and carries them off on his shoulders.
beats.label: GAZA'S GATE

beats.text: Destination: the hill facing Hebron, roughly sixty kilometres in a straight line.
beats.say: Destination: the hill facing HEB-ron, roughly sixty kilometres in a straight line.

beats.text: Hebron sits about nine hundred metres above Gaza: uphill.
beats.say: HEB-ron sits about nine hundred metres above Gaza: uphill.

beats.text: What's not proven: the exact hill. The Hebrew can mean 'facing' Hebron, not at it.
beats.say: What's not proven: the exact hill. The Hebrew can mean 'facing' HEB-ron, not at it.

beats.text: He grew up in Zorah, fell for a woman in Timnah, and struck thirty men at Ashkelon.
beats.say: He grew up in ZOR-ah, fell for a woman in TIM-nah, and struck thirty men at ASH-keh-lon.

beats.text: Later, captured and blinded, he grinds grain in a Gaza prison.
There, Philistines gather in the temple of Dagon to celebrate.
beats.say: There, FILL-iss-teens gather in the temple of DAY-gon to celebrate.

beats.text: Judges says about three thousand people watch from the roof.
beats.label: ~3,000 ON THE ROOF

beats.text: Samson pushes the two middle pillars, and the building comes down.
Zorah to Gaza is nearly sixty kilometres. His world is small; his legend is big.
beats.say: ZOR-ah to Gaza is nearly sixty kilometres. His world is small; his legend is big.

beats.text: A gate, a hill, a temple: legend, memory, or both?

youtube.title: Samson Carried a City Gate 60 km? 🗺️ #shorts
youtube.description:
From Gaza's gate to the hill facing Hebron: roughly 60 km straight-line, and uphill. Legend or memory?
The exact hill is not proven; the Hebrew can mean 'facing' Hebron.
#Samson #Judges #BibleHistory #MythUnearthed
